### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-queue`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 82 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **54** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ce7db3284f7454884499476ac1f28c672b7e0d1f` — the merge of head `f94bcab7d35570caf826930c52a256f40efadaae` into base `077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ce7db3284f7454884499476ac1f28c672b7e0d1f && git checkout ce7db3284f7454884499476ac1f28c672b7e0d1f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881 f94bcab7d35570caf826930c52a256f40efadaae && git checkout -B drift-repro 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881 && git merge --no-ff f94bcab7d35570caf826930c52a256f40efadaae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 077831538950da0af7b31c5fdafa2463caaa9881` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `dbe4ac7ac20b52bb48b36b1b5a96769a58cac8b5`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset); no published schema and no governed path in the file list, so no ④. Inputs: card #37705 with every comment, this PR's body and 8-file net diff against `main` (merge-base `0f8e13b0`), and the head's check-runs (57 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, none pending; all eleven required contexts green). The PR is still a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`ObjectQL.runOutsideOpenUnits(body)` (new public member on an exported class): right.** It is a one-line delegate to the existing `runOutsideOpenUnits(txStore, undefined, body)` in `unit-detach.ts`: it leaves the engine's ambient unit entry and records that entry's handle as detached. No handle is threaded, which is correct here because the store's statements carry `SYSTEM_CTX` and no `transaction`. Nothing that is already accepted changes.
- **The detach matches the async-hook exit only for `afterFind`, not for the write events.** `engine-scoped-context.ts` sends a write event's `async` run through `runOutsideOpenUnitsOnCommit`: it waits for the unit's commit and is dropped on rollback (#33760). The new member starts at once and is never dropped. That is a deliberate choice, and the changeset and the docblock state it. F-1 grades the result.
- **`SuspendedRunStoreEngine.runOutsideOpenUnits?` (optional member on an exported type): right.** The registered `objectql` and `data` services are both the `ObjectQL` instance, so the shipped composition takes the detached arm. A double without units keeps the old in-place write. `recordTerminal` drops `async` but still returns `writeTerminal`'s promise, and its only caller (`run-history.ts`, `void write.catch`) never awaits it. So no single-connection pool can deadlock on a detached write that a caller is awaiting.
- **No write that must be atomic with the triggering write escapes.** Only the terminal history row (find, upsert, retention prune) is detached. The run's own node writes, the pause write and the suspension claim stay in the unit, awaited. Paused rows (raw `runId`) and terminal rows (`run_` + runId) are disjoint, so a detached upsert cannot race the unit's claim delete on the same row.
- **`DispatchLoop` ticks in its constructor's async context: right, and safe for context.** All four in-tree loops (notification, HTTP delivery, DB queue, audit sealer) are constructed at boot (constructor, `start()` from `kernel:ready`, or plugin start). None of their ticks reads an ambient store, because delivery rows carry their own tenant and recipient. Timer-driven ticks never had the waker's context anyway, so no delivery depended on it. `start()`, `wake()`, `wakeAt()` with a past due time, and a future `wakeAt()` timer are all re-homed. The `node:async_hooks` import matches the `node:crypto` and `node:net` imports already on core's main entry.
- **Root cause and coverage of the reproduction: right for the two producers measured.** The card's audit failures are the `sys_activity` rows that the notification tick's delivery updates fire. The PR measured 0 "Transaction query already complete" lines in hotcrm with the fix. F-4 names other candidates of the same class.
- **Tests: they fail without the fix, by reading.** objectql: with `return body()`, the detached read takes the unit's handle (`seen` equals `[begun[0]]`), and the inner `transaction()` joins the outer unit (`begun` length 1). Both cases go red and the CONTROL stays green. service-automation: without the routing, every statement records `outside: false`, so 2 cases go red. core: without `loopTickAtHome`, the tick sees the waker's store, so 2 cases go red. That matches the reported 6/6.
- **Read-after-write sweep: it holds for `sys_automation_run`.** Every listed reader of the durable row already waits with a bound (10 s, 100 × 20 ms, 50 × 100 ms) or reads the in-memory log. The unlisted readers I checked read rows that are not the terminal write of a run fired inside a unit: schedule-fired runs, restored-approval `hasSuspendedRun`, stubbed runtime doors. Test Core and Dogfood Regression are green on this head. The sweep's DispatchLoop sentence does not hold on every driver: see F-2.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/core` at `patch`. The diff publishes one new public method, one new optional interface member and a tick-context change. It adds no authorable key, no accepted value and no metadata type, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, and under the level rule a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The level is right.
- `Clause-②:` the PR body and the changeset each carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at the start of a line. That is right for a public member added to an exported class with no signature or input narrowed. The card's `Clause-②: no` was filed before the fix existed, and the PR correctly supersedes it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F-1 · nit: the terminal row now outlives a rolled-back triggering write.** On a pooled driver it can also commit before that write is visible. A `completed` history row can therefore name a run whose in-unit effects were rolled back, and a `trigger_record_id` can name a row that is not yet visible. The changeset and the `unit-detach.ts` docblock declare this. It is defensible: a run whose failure caused the rollback must keep its row, which the commit-and-drop posture of #33760 would erase. Accepted as a deviation; nothing is owed in this PR.
- **F-2 · should-fix: a wake made inside a unit can no longer see the row it was woken for, on a pooled driver.** The woken tick now runs outside the unit, so on Postgres or MySQL it cannot see the outbox or queue row the uncommitted unit just enqueued, and `nextDueAt` cannot see it either. The tick finds nothing, and the row waits for the next backoff tick: twice `intervalMs` by default, and `maxIdleIntervalMs` (30 s by default) when `soleWriter` is set, whose premise is that wakes carry the work. On a single-connection pool, which is the hotcrm case, the tick waits for the connection and sees the committed row. So the sweep's sentence that `sys_activity` and delivery rows "land when they did" holds only there. Close this either way: (a) the wake fires on the unit's commit, which the producer that enqueues through the engine can arrange; or (b) correct the PR body and changeset to state the pooled-driver latency, and file it as a follow-up card under the filing gate.
- **F-3 · should-fix: the card is not delivered whole by `Fixes #37705`.** The card's acceptance also requires hotcrm's six lead_assignment tests to pass on the release that carries the fix, and that cannot be observed at merge. The PR body also says three hotcrm `case_escalation` reads, which passed on `main`, need the file's own bounded wait (`landedRuns`) because of this change. No card tracks either item. Before ACCEPT: file the hotcrm-side card for the three reads, and either switch to `Refs #37705` so the card stays open until the release check, or record on the card that the hotcrm card owns that check.
- **F-4 · nit: candidates of the same class, outside the diff.** `plugin-audit`'s read-audit and dataset-query-audit batchers are enqueued from a synchronous `afterFind` (`recordView`). The batcher calls `void runFlush()` at `maxBatchSize` and arms its flush timer in the reader's async context. A user-principal read inside an open unit can therefore start a `sys_audit_log` persist enrolled in that unit, which can then outlive it. This is unmeasured and needs a reproduction before a card (Prime Directive 10). The PR body already names `runOutsideOpenUnits` as the exit for the next such producer.
- **F-5 · nit: the loop's home is wherever it was constructed.** Every in-tree construction runs at boot. But `DbQueueAdapter.start()` is also reachable from `subscribe()` under `autoStart`, and a lazy first subscribe inside a request would make that request's context the loop's home for good. A sentence in the `DispatchLoop` docblock naming the boot-construction invariant would close this.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. The in-app sort and per-row delete in `pruneFlowOverflow` predate the diff; it is only re-routed here.
- Dev flags and open questions: the PR body's two flags are answered above. The missing framework end-to-end twin is acceptable, because the engine pin holds the race by construction (the driver holds the read until after the commit). The hotcrm three-line change is F-3. The report carries no `open_questions` entry. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.
- Remaining before ACCEPT: close F-2 and F-3 (each a delta read by this reviewer), then take the PR out of draft.
